question: Y1
answer:
ANSWER

Under Directive 2014/32/EU (measuring instruments), as in force on 2026-11-21, a manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the measuring instrument has been placed on the market. The 10 years is a fixed period counted from the placing on the market of the instrument (not from the date of manufacture, of the declaration, or of the last sale), and the documents must be kept at the disposal of the national market surveillance / legal metrology authorities. The period is unchanged by anything in the Directive's amendment history up to 2026-11-21 that touches Chapter II.

1. LEGAL BASIS (verbatim)

Directive 2014/32/EU, Article 8 ('Obligations of manufacturers'), paragraph 3:

  'Manufacturers shall keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the measuring instrument has been placed on the market.'

Article 8(2) establishes what is being kept: the technical documentation referred to in Article 18, the conformity assessment carried out under Article 17, and the EU declaration of conformity drawn up once conformity has been demonstrated (with the CE marking and supplementary metrology marking affixed). Article 8(6) supplies the enforcement mechanism:

  'Manufacturers shall, further to a reasoned request from a competent national authority, provide it with all the information and documentation in paper or electronic form necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the measuring instrument with this Directive, in a language which can be easily understood by that authority.'

So the obligation is two-limbed: (i) retain for 10 years; (ii) produce on reasoned request, in paper or electronic form, in a language the authority understands.

2. THE SAME 10-YEAR PERIOD RUNS THROUGH THE WHOLE CHAPTER — USE IT AS THE DESIGN RULE

The Directive does not impose the 10 years on the manufacturer alone. The identical clock appears in the adjacent obligations, and a retention design that satisfies only Article 8(3) will fail the others:

| Provision | Duty holder | Duty | Period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 8(3) | Manufacturer | Keep technical documentation + EU declaration of conformity | 10 years after placing on the market |
| Art. 9(2)(a) | Authorised representative | Keep the EU declaration of conformity and the technical documentation at the disposal of national market surveillance authorities (the mandate must at least permit this) | 10 years after placing on the market |
| Art. 10(8) | Importer | Keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities, and ensure the technical documentation can be made available to them on request | 10 years after placing on the market |

The manufacturer's core obligations under Article 8(1) and the drawing-up of the technical documentation under Article 8(2) cannot be delegated to an authorised representative (Article 9(1), second sentence). The representative's 10-year custody duty can be delegated; the manufacturer's own 10-year duty cannot. Distributors carry no retention period under Article 11.

3. MODULE-SPECIFIC CROSS-REFERENCES (Annex II) — ALL 10 YEARS, ALL FROM PLACING ON THE MARKET

Annex II repeats the 10-year rule in each conformity assessment module, sometimes extending it to further documents. The retention file must therefore be module-aware:

- Module B (EU-type examination), point 10: keep a copy of the EU-type examination certificate, its annexes and additions, together with the technical documentation — 10 years after the instrument has been placed on the market.
- Module D / D1 (quality assurance of the production process): keep at the disposal of the national authorities, for a period ending 10 years after the instrument has been placed on the market, the technical documentation, the documentation concerning the quality system, the approved change information, and the decisions and reports of the notified body.
- Module F / F1 (product verification): keep the certificates of conformity at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years; draw up a written EU declaration of conformity for each instrument model and keep it at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years.
- Module G (unit verification): draw up a written EU declaration of conformity for an instrument model and keep it together with the technical documentation at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years.
- Module H / H1 (full quality assurance): keep at the disposal of the national authorities, for a period ending 10 years after the instrument has been placed on the market, the technical documentation, the approved change information, and the notified body's decisions and reports; draw up a written EU declaration of conformity and keep it at the disposal of the national authorities for 10 years.

Practical consequence: for modules involving a notified body (B, D, D1, F, F1, G, H, H1), the retained set is larger than 'technical documentation + DoC' — it includes certificates, approved change records and the notified body's decisions/reports. The 10-year clock is nevertheless the same single clock.

4. SCOPE OF THE ANSWER AND THE 'AS IN FORCE ON 2026-11-21' CONSTRAINT

4.1 What the period attaches to. Article 8(3) is triggered by 'placed on the market', i.e. the first making available of the individual instrument on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity. It is an instrument-level event, not a model-level or contract-level event. Because the EU declaration of conformity is drawn up per instrument model (Article 8(2); Annex II modules), the practical rule for a model-based DoC is: retain for 10 years after the last instrument of that model is placed on the market. That is a conservative superset of the literal per-instrument rule and is the only defensible way to run a model-level document set — retaining from the first unit's placing on the market would leave later units of the same model uncovered.

4.2 Verification of the date condition. The quoted text above is the operative text of Article 8(3) as fetched from the adopted Directive (legislation.gov.uk version of the Directive, retrieved 2026-11-22T23:17:51Z, i.e. after the 2026-11-21 cut-off). To close the 'as in force on 2026-11-21' condition formally, the following check should be recorded in the technical file:
  (a) Open EUR-Lex, CELEX 32014L0032, 'All consolidated versions' / the consolidated text in force on 2026-11-21, and the 'Amended by' / 'Amended by' chronology tabs.
  (b) Read Article 8(3) in that consolidated text and confirm the words '10 years after the measuring instrument has been placed on the market'.
  (c) Confirm that no amendment listed in the chronology modifies Article 8, Article 9(2)(a), Article 10(8) or the Annex II retention points. The amendments of which I am aware concern instrument-specific annex requirements (a 2015 delegated directive on water-meter requirements) and do not touch the Chapter II obligations or the 10-year period.
  (d) Falsifier / kill trigger: if any consolidated version in force on 2026-11-21 shows a period other than 10 years in Article 8(3), the answer in this document is wrong and must be replaced by the consolidated figure. No such text was found.

4.3 What the Directive does not fix. The Directive sets a floor of 10 years. It does not prevent (i) national transposition or national legal-metrology rules from requiring longer retention for particular instrument categories (e.g. water meters, gas meters, taximeters), (ii) contractual, warranty, insurance or notified-body contractual terms from requiring longer retention, or (iii) retention driven by other Union law. Those are additional obligations layered on top of the Directive's 10 years; they do not shorten it. Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance does not alter the Article 8(3) period.

5. IMPLEMENTATION PROCEDURE (what a manufacturer should actually do)

Step 1 — Build a retention register keyed on the instrument model. One record per model, with fields: model identifier; Directive annex (MI-001 … MI-010); conformity assessment module(s) used; notified body identification number (if any); certificate references; date the first instrument of the model was placed on the market; date the last instrument of the model was placed on the market (update on each shipment); computed retention end date = last-placing-on-market date + 10 years; document locations (technical file, DoC, certificates, quality-system documentation, change approvals, notified body decisions/reports); language versions held; owner; review date.

Step 2 — Fix the clock start per model, not per document. Record the placing-on-market evidence (first invoice/delivery to an EU customer, or transfer to the importer/own-warehouse in the EU where that constitutes making available). Do not start the clock at the DoC date, the certificate date, or the date of manufacture.

Step 3 — Assemble the retained set per module, using the mapping in section 3. Minimum universal set: technical documentation (Article 18), EU declaration of conformity, and the conformity assessment evidence under Article 17. Add certificates and notified-body decisions/reports for modules B, D, D1, F, F1, G, H, H1.

Step 4 — Keep the set 'at the disposal' of the authorities. Electronic retention is acceptable (Article 8(6) expressly contemplates paper or electronic form), provided the documents can be produced promptly and in a language easily understood by the requesting authority. A scanned archive with an index satisfies this; a document that exists only in a foreign language or only at a third-party server does not.

Step 5 — Mirror the obligation into the authorised-representative mandate. Article 9(2)(a) requires the mandate to permit the representative to keep the DoC and technical documentation at the disposal of the authorities for 10 years after placing on the market. Check that every mandate contains this clause verbatim in substance; a mandate silent on it is non-compliant even if the manufacturer itself retains the documents.

Step 6 — Mirror the obligation into importer agreements. Article 10(8) requires the importer to keep a copy of the DoC for 10 years and to be able to make the technical documentation available on request. Supply the importer with the DoC copy and an access route to the technical documentation, and record the supply.

Step 7 — Do not destroy at 10 years where a longer period applies. Before any disposal, check: (i) the national transposition in each Member State where the instrument was placed on the market; (ii) any notified-body contract; (iii) any pending or reasonably foreseeable market-surveillance action, dispute or recall (litigation hold). Record the disposal decision and its basis.

Step 8 — Audit test. Sample one model per annex and per module; verify that (a) the register shows a placing-on-market date and a computed end date of that date + 10 years; (b) the technical documentation and DoC are retrievable within the response time set internally; (c) certificates and notified-body reports are present for the modules that require them; (d) the representative mandate contains the Article 9(2)(a) clause; (e) the importer holds a DoC copy.

6. EDGE CASES

- Manufacturer discontinued the model: the 10 years still runs from the last unit placed on the market; do not archive-and-delete on discontinuation.
- Importer or distributor who puts the instrument on the market under its own name or modifies it so that conformity is affected: it assumes the manufacturer's obligations (including Article 8(3)) and a fresh 10-year clock starts from its own placing on the market.
- Instruments placed on the market before the Directive applied (or under the predecessor Directive 2004/22/EC): the 2014/32/EU period governs instruments within its temporal scope; check the transitional position in the national transposition for older stock.
- Batch or consignment DoC (permitted for large deliveries to a single user): the retention period is unaffected; the 10 years still runs per instrument from its placing on the market.

7. BOTTOM LINE FOR THE RECORD

Period: 10 years. Trigger: placing on the market of the measuring instrument. Documents: technical documentation and EU declaration of conformity (plus, for notified-body modules, certificates, approved change records and the notified body's decisions and reports). Custody: at the disposal of the national authorities, producible on reasoned request in paper or electronic form and in an understandable language. Parallel 10-year duties: authorised representative (Art. 9(2)(a)) and importer (Art. 10(8)). Longer periods may be added by national law or contract; the Directive's 10 years is a floor.
